content.text:
The sleep finished and printed `first-done`.

Clouds form when water vapor in rising air cools until it condenses into tiny droplets or ice crystals around particles like dust or salt. Their shapes depend on how the air moves: cumulus clouds are puffy and piled up from convection on warm days, while stratus clouds are flat, grey sheets that spread across the sky. Higher up, cirrus clouds are thin, wispy ice crystals that often signal a change in weather.

Clouds do more than decorate the sky. They reflect sunlight back to space and trap heat radiating from the ground, so they shape both daytime temperatures and nighttime warmth. They also move water around the planet, since precipitation falls from them and returns to rivers, lakes, and oceans. Because of this, cloud cover is one of the hardest things for climate models to represent accurately.

One fish: salmon.

message.content: Write a numbered list of 40 facts about the ocean, one line each, no tools.

content.text:
1. The ocean covers about 71% of Earth's surface.
2. The ocean holds roughly 97% of the planet's water.
3. The average depth of the ocean is about 3,700 meters (12,100 feet).
4. The deepest known point, the Challenger Deep, is about 11,000 meters below sea level.
5. More than 80% of the ocean has never been mapped in detail.
6. The ocean produces roughly half of the oxygen we breathe, mostly through phytoplankton.
7. Phytoplankton are microscopic algae that form the base of most marine food webs.
8. The ocean absorbs about a quarter of the carbon dioxide humans emit each year.
9. Seawater averages about 3.5% salt by mass.
10. The ocean's salinity varies by region, with the Red Sea among the saltiest large bodies of water.
11. The ocean's average surface temperature is around 17°C (62°F), though it varies widely by latitude.
12. Sunlight penetrates only about 200 meters into the ocean, so the deep sea is in permanent darkness.
13. Around 90% of the ocean's water lies in the deep sea below 1,000 meters.
14. The ocean is connected as one global system of currents, often called the global conveyor belt.
15. Ocean currents redistribute heat and help regulate Earth's climate.
16. Tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon, with the Sun contributing as well.
17. The largest waves ever measured were over 25 meters (80 feet) high.
18. The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean basin.
19. The Pacific covers more area than all of Earth's land combined.
20. The Atlantic Ocean is widening slowly as tectonic plates pull apart.
21. The Great Barrier Reef, off Australia, is the largest coral reef system in the world.
22. Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but support about 25% of known marine species.
23. The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived, and it feeds in the ocean.
24. Some whales can dive more than 2,000 meters in search of food.
25. Giant squid have the largest eyes of any animal, roughly the size of a dinner plate.
26. Some deep-sea animals produce their own light through bioluminescence.
27. Over 80% of marine life is estimated to be unknown to science.
28. Hydrothermal vents on the seafloor support ecosystems that do not rely on sunlight.
29. The ocean contains an estimated 20 million tons of gold dissolved in seawater, but it is extremely dilute.
30. Ocean noise from shipping and sonar can affect how whales and dolphins communicate.
31. Sea otters use rocks as tools to crack open shellfish.
32. Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.
33. Sharks have existed in the oceans for more than 400 million years, predating trees.
34. The Mariana Trench is over 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) long.
35. Plastic debris has been found in every major ocean basin, including the deep sea.
36. Mangroves, seagrass, and salt marshes store large amounts of carbon, often called "blue carbon."
37. Sea level rise is driven partly by thermal expansion, as warmer water takes up more space.
38. Many marine species migrate thousands of kilometers each year, including sea turtles and some tuna.
39. Bioluminescent plankton can make waves glow blue at night in some coastal areas.
40. Humans have explored only a tiny fraction of the deep ocean directly, and most of it remains unseen.
